The standard edition is Koenen & Römer 1988 (editio minor), built on Henrichs & Koenen, ZPE 1975–82 (editio maior with German translation). Photos and diplomatic text: Koenen & Römer 1985 (PTA 35).
Copyright: the 1988 book is still in print (Springer/VS reprint). Its German translation, commentary and apparatus are under copyright (Römer is living; Koenen and Henrichs are deceased, so their estates hold it). The constituted Greek text itself: in Germany, scientific editions under §70 UrhG are protected for only 25 years from publication, which lapsed around 2013 for the 1988 edition and earlier for the ZPE edition. In the US, an editor's supplements give at most thin protection. Using the Greek with fresh translation is therefore low-risk, but the claim "the critical text is under copyright" is overstated.
Best open source: the Unicode Greek of the editio minor in the Lieu/Vermes CFM draft at manichaeism.de. It is freely downloadable but carries no open licence and is a work in progress.
ZPE 1975–82 issues are not in the free uni-koeln ZPE download archive (they are on JSTOR). I found no public-domain digitised text.
LLM feasibility is moderate to low. The tiny pages are full of lacunae and editors' supplements, and the later half (about pp. 100–192) is very fragmentary. A good translation has to follow the 1988 apparatus and Römer's later readings.

- Siculus Flaccus, De condicionibus agrorum, complete (Russian has only about 5–6 pp. of excerpts);

Translate from Thulin 1913 (public domain) and have the editor check readings against Campbell and Guillaumin.

series:schole-philosophy.notes:
Coverage and limits.
(1) ΣΧΟΛΗ: I went through the issue pages for vols 1.1–20.2 (2007–2026) on the official site (classics.nsu.ru/schole) and the Russian "Переводы" archive for 2007–2019. The listing should be near-complete. Two corrections to the site: (a) the site labels ΣΧΟΛΗ 16.2: 862–888 as "Maximus of Tyre Or. 8–9", but the PDF is actually Garadja's translation of Ptolemy Chennus' Novel History (Photius cod. 190); Maximus Or. 8–9 is in 16.1: 317–333. (b) Dicaearchus appears as 10.1 on the English page, but the PDF and the Russian page give 11.1 (2017): 271–282.
Exclusions from ΣΧΟΛΗ: translations of modern scholarship (Dodds, Rist, Burkert, O'Brien, O'Meara, Brisson); Renaissance and later texts (Ficino, Paracelsus, Hugh of Saint-Cher, Pico); Kydones' Greek version of Aquinas (20.2), an edition and study with no clear Russian translation. Also left out are articles in the TRANSLATIONS sections that I could not confirm contain a translation: 16.1 "Moses Attikidzon", 15.2 "Group portrait of the sophists", 19.2 "Philo and Pythagorean texts".
(2) Платоновские исследования: checked the tables of contents of issues 1–24 (2014–2026/1). Only items in the translation sections and other clear translations are listed. Ficino, Pico, Averroes, Ibn Taymiyya, Guillaume de Leus, Nicholas Bonet and Isaac of Stella are excluded as medieval or Renaissance.
(3) Историко-философский ежегодник: checked against the journal's site (ife.iphras.ru, 41 issue pages) and the 1986–2016 publication list on CyberLeninka. I found no translations of ancient texts in the 2017–2025 volumes. Liber de causis (1990) is excluded as medieval Arabic/Latin. For Plotinus I 8 (1989) the sources disagree on the translator: the published bibliography says Т.Ю. Бородай, the journal site credits М.К. Трофимова. The 1989 Sidorov article on Philoponus' "Arbiter" fragments is an article, not a separate translation, so it is excluded.
(4) Вестник РХГА: checked the journal's own archive for 2018–2026 and found no ancient translations. For 2007–2017 I used CyberLeninka searches only, so the coverage of 2016–2018 Augustine items may be partial; earlier years were not checked systematically.
(5) «Ψυχή»: I could not confirm that any Russian journal by this name publishes translations (CyberLeninka returned nothing). It may be a confusion with ΕΙΝΑΙ (St Petersburg), which I did not check.
(6) Book series «Платоновское наследие» / «Библиотека платоновского общества»: I could not confirm either series exists. The web-search budget was used up and DuckDuckGo returned a CAPTCHA. Instead I listed the confirmed ΣΧΟΛΗ Supplements series (vols II, III, V, VII, VIII; vols I, IV, VI are not ancient texts). Russian book translations of Hermias, Olympiodorus, Proclus In Parm. etc. outside these venues were not covered.
(7) Topic gaps: in these venues I found no translations of Hierocles, Stoic fragments (other than Seneca in IFE), Ammonius, Hermias, Philoponus or Alexander of Aphrodisias, except Alexander's text carrying Aristotle's De ideis (Платоновские исследования 24, 2026).

KEY FINDINGS on Latyshev (vol. I index): NO Constantine Porphyrogenitus, NO Suda lexicon section. The 'Σουίδας' at p. 886 is the historian Suidas (Thessalika), not the lexicon; Suda glosses are only cited as sources for fragments. Tzetzes appears only as commentator on Lycophron (pp. 400-406); no separate Chiliades entry. Jordanes is not in vol. II. Ps.-Callisthenes is pp. 897-904 and Iulius Valerius / Itinerarium Alexandri vol. II p. 311 (relevant to Alexander Romance).

Gaps and caveats:
(1) I could not place each Latyshev author in a specific VDI 1947-49 issue. Most of those PDFs are scans with no text layer, so for Latyshev items the URL points to the archive.org original and the page numbers are vol. I/II pages.
(2) Not every VDI translation is listed. Excluded: purely Near Eastern, Egyptian, Iranian and Chinese items (except the Urartu dossiers); reviews of book translations; and articles that only quote passages. Some 1946-1952 supplements (Appian 1950, Sallust 1950, Pliny NH 'technology' 1946 No.3) have contents or translators confirmed only partly. For Frontinus 1946 the page names only А.Б. Ранович as author of the introduction; that he also translated the text is attributed from secondary citation and is unverified here.
(3) 'Античные свидетельства о Северном Причерноморье': I could not verify that a book with this exact title exists. Search engines were captcha-blocked or rate-limited, and the rusneb and Google Books APIs were blocked. series:patristic-byzantine.notes:
I found 103 items. I checked each one against a table of contents, an article's metadata, a CyberLeninka record or an azbyka source note.

Method: WebSearch had already used up its 200-call quota. Bing, DuckDuckGo, Yandex, Mojeek and Brave all returned CAPTCHAs or junk, and elibrary.ru refused access. So nothing came from open search; everything came from site-level harvesting.

Fully scanned:
- Библия и христианская древность: all issues 2019–2026, from the patristic.ru archive.
- Метафраст: all 9 issues.
- Богословский вестник: 53 issues on the MDA OJS (publishing.mpda.ru).
- Богословские труды: tables of contents for vols. 30–51.

Searched only by keyword:
- Вестник ПСТГУ, Христианское чтение, Труды и переводы (СПбДА), Вестник ЕДС, Труды Нижегородской ДС and Вестник Оренбургской ДС, through the CyberLeninka search API.
- The azbyka.ru author pages and the azbyka full-text search.
- Bibliographies in Православная энциклопедия articles (Eusebius, Didymus).

Not scanned: Scrinium; Византийский временник; Церковь и время beyond the Eusebius item; the publisher catalogues of Сретенский монастырь, ПСТГУ, Абышко, «Святоотеческое наследие» and «Смирение».

No post-1990 Russian translation located (these are negative findings within the sources above, not proof of absence):
- Didymus: only the 1870 De Spiritu Sancto, reprinted 1999.
- Asterius Sophista's Psalm homilies: only архим. Модест, 1911, under the name of Asterius of Amasea.
- Quodvultdeus.
- Zeno of Verona: only pieces in Христианское чтение, 1843.
- Facundus: only excerpts in Доброклонский, 1880.
- Sophronius' Miracles of Cyrus and John: only an excerpt in Душеполезное чтение, 1889.
- Ps.-Clementines.
- Hippolytus' Chronicon.
- George Synkellos (only studies of the Slavonic version).
- John of Antioch the historian.
- Eusebius: Demonstratio, the Isaiah commentary, and Chronicon Book I (Armenian).

Partial coverage only: Zonaras exists only in the Khvalkov sections of books XI–XIV. For Malalas, only Bolgov's Book XIII is itemized. Bolgov reports Samutkina's translations from books XIV–XVII and Chekalova's of book XVIII, but I could not verify their exact citations, so they are not listed. Julius Africanus exists only in a translation from the English ANF.

Items flagged as weak or uncertain:
- Cyril's Contra Iulianum (Франжев, azbyka 2026): extent not verified.
- Ambrosiaster on ekzeget.ru: anonymous, no imprint, known only from Лысевич's dissertation.
- Cosmas and Damian: the translation dates from 1972 and was only reissued in 1994/1995, so it predates 1990.
- Russian ACCS: excerpts only, mostly translated from English.
- Arelate preachers volume (2004): the sermon translators' names were not visible; I give the editor, Fokin.
- «Разъяснение догматов»: the BV issue (№20–21, 2016) comes from OJS metadata.

The pravenc.ru entry for Eusebius (https://www.pravenc.ru/text/187357.html) gives Yastrebov's Church and Time citation and his 1999/2001 fragments.

Also seen but not itemized: the Shperl Joshua homilies (no source note on azbyka), and dissertation fragments (Мурилкин 2020; Зайцев 2007 on Hippolytus).

verify:crit_013.recommendation: Keep at priority 3, as a candidate on the Russian axis only. The Russian gap is genuine. The text is uniquely valuable: it is the main witness to Methodist medicine and to the lost Soranus, and it preserves material on Asclepiades, Themison, Erasistratus, Diocles and Praxagoras, plus Parmenides B18. It fails priority 2, because full English (Drabkin 1950) and full German (Pape, CML 1990-93) translations exist, though both are in copyright, so an open RU+EN version still adds something. Translating the whole work is not realistic: it runs to about 143k Latin words of difficult late-Latin technical prose. Instead, pilot one self-contained chapter, using Drabkin and Pape as validation cross-checks. Candidates (section ranges approximate): Tard. I 5, 'De furore sive insania' (mania, roughly §§144-183); Cel. I (phrenitis, with its polemic against Asclepiades and Themison); or Cel. III on hydrophobia (roughly §§98-137). Use the DigilibLT/Bendz text (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IT). Its terms suit a non-commercial project, but Neoscholia's derived bilingual outputs would have to be released BY-NC-SA. The Amman 1709/1722 edition can serve as a fully public-domain fallback. Before starting, check whether Volkova (St Petersburg State University) has a Russian translation in progress.

verify:crit_014.source_text: The best public-domain base is Th. Mommsen (ed.), Chronographus anni CCCLIIII, MGH Auctores antiquissimi 9 (Chronica minora I), Berlin 1892, pp. 13-148. It is public domain, and free scans are on dMGH. The Liber generationis is at pp. 78/89-140 in parallel columns, and the Chronica urbis Romae is at the end of the volume. For the calendar there is also CIL I² (1893), public domain. tertullian.org has a full digital Latin transcription of all 16 parts, which Pearse states is public domain ("copy freely"), so it is directly usable as machine-readable input. Modern standard editions: Divjak–Wischmeyer 2014 is in copyright but available open access under CC BY-NC; it covers parts 1-13 and not 14-16, and Burgess (ZAC 21, 2017, doi:10.1515/zac-2017-0020) criticises it heavily. Burgess 2014 (in copyright) is the standard edition of the Chronica urbis Romae. Degrassi, Inscriptiones Italiae XIII.2 (1963), is the standard edition of the calendar and is in copyright. For the Greek background of the Liber generationis, Bauer–Helm, GCS Hippolytus IV (2nd ed., 1955), is in copyright. Recommended working text: Mommsen 1892 plus the tertullian.org transcription, with Burgess and Divjak–Wischmeyer consulted for corrections only.
verify:crit_014.research_yield: Moderate to high. The search confirmed the claimed Russian gap: no translation of any part turned up, only fragmentary quotations in articles. It also corrected the English picture. The tertullian.org translation is partial: the Liber generationis is explicitly left untranslated, the city chronicle is incomplete, and the lists are given in Latin. The Chronica urbis Romae is fully translated in Burgess 2014, and a Liber generationis (probably recension I) in Hoover 2025, both in copyright. The Divjak–Wischmeyer edition turned out to have no translation. Limitations: the WebSearch budget was exhausted, and Bing, DuckDuckGo, Yandex and Google were blocked or returned junk. The Russian check therefore relied on CyberLeninka, the Wikipedia API and targeted sites; elibrary, the RSL catalogue, ВДИ indexes and Latyshev's table of contents remain unverified.
verify:crit_014.recommendation: Keep as a Russian-first project: a first annotated Russian translation of the whole Chronograph is a real gap. Work in modules ordered by value. (1) Chronica urbis Romae (Part 16): short prose, rich in anecdote, ideal as a pilot unit. Mommsen MGH AA 9 is public domain; use Burgess 2014 for checking. (2) Liber generationis II, the Chronograph's own recension continued to 334 with the Bulgars line (Part 15). It has no English rendering on tertullian.org and possibly none anywhere if Hoover translates only recension I, so it could be an open-licence first in English too. (3) Catalogus Liberianus, the two Depositiones, the 14 Regions. (4) Calendar, fasti, prefects and Easter table as glossed tables, which are cheap for an LLM but add little. The value for English is limited because Burgess and Hoover exist; frame the English output as the first open, complete translation of the whole Chronograph rather than a first translation. The editor's Latin expertise fits well. Before committing, check Hoover 2025 for which recension it uses, and Latyshev SC II and ЛИБИ I for excerpts.

Merobaudis quae supersunt» plus the praefatio «De Merobaudis codice editionibusque»). Older public-domain editions: B.G. Niebuhr, St Gall 1823 and Bonn ²1824 (https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_MbZDAAAAYAAJ); I. Bekker, CSHB «Merobaudes et Corippus», Bonn 1836 (https://archive.org/details/merobaudesetcor00bekkgoog). De Christo (30 hexameters, authenticity doubted): Riese, Anthologia Latina 878 (1870), PL 61 and Birt's Claudian (MGH AA 10, 1892), all public domain. Modern critical texts are in copyright: Bruzzone 1999 (Pan. II), Bruzzone 2018 (Pan. I), Clover 1971 (APS, which reprints Vollmer's text), and the unpublished Ploton-Nicollet 2008. Size is very small: Pan. II about 200 lacunose hexameters, Pan. I prose fragments of a few pages, Carm. 1–4 (24, 14, and two short pieces) and De Christo 30 lines. The single St Gall palimpsest (Stiftsbibliothek 908) leaves many lacunae and conjectures, so the text should be checked against Bruzzone's readings.

The corpus is tiny, historically valuable (contemporary praise of Aetius and Valentinian III, ecphrases of the Ravenna palace) and, as far as I could find, has no Russian translation in any series. It is not an English 'first': Clover 1971 is complete for the St Gall texts. A new English version would only add value for De Christo, if Clover indeed omits it (still to verify), or as a modern annotated rendering. Base text: Vollmer, MGH AA 14 (1905, public domain, dMGH). Collate with Bruzzone 1999 and 2018 for the restored lacunae, citing her conjectures but not reproducing her text. Mark the palimpsest gaps clearly and present De Christo as of disputed authorship. LLM feasibility is moderate: the Latin is short but mannered and lacunose, so the editor should review every restored passage. series:vostlit.notes:
I collected these by crawling vostlit.info directly with curl. Sources were all 28 alphabetical author indexes (А–Я), the regional "Документы" indexes and the ru.wikipedia list of «Памятники письменности Востока» volumes. The regional indexes checked were Византия (which on vostlit also covers late antiquity), Италия, Испания, Иран, Кавказ, Египет and Аравия. vostlit has no Rome or antiquity index. I opened about 300 text pages and took the translator, year and venue from each page's «Текст воспроизведен по изданию» line.

How "partial" and "complete" were judged:
- "Partial" means excerpts. Many vostlit Greek and Latin items are only the Scythia/Caucasus extracts from Латышев's «Известия древних писателей о Скифии и Кавказе» (ВДИ 1947–1952). Others come from the «Древние славяне в отрывках…» (ВДИ 1941) compilation, from Тер-Мкртичян's «Армянские источники о Средней Азии» (1979/1985), or from Шмидт's 1958 Arabic and Persian excerpts.
- Treat those Latyshev-excerpt authors as not translated in full on vostlit, even where full Russian translations exist elsewhere (for example Ammianus by Кулаковский–Сонни, Theophylact by Пигулевская 1957, Agathangelos 2004).
- I excluded entries that only have «Заметка» or «Рецензия» pages, because these are reviews of editions, not translations. That rules out George Synkellos, Glykas, Tzetzes, Eutychius, Kartlis tskhovreba, Ilya bar Shinaya, Nikephoros Kallistos, Symeon Logothete, Yohannan bar Penkaye, the Continuatio Prosperi, John Lydus and the Geoponika.

Gaps and uncertain points:
- I did not list post-7th-century Byzantine documents, hagiography or law in detail. The Byzantium index has about 320 entries, most of them medieval.
- I omitted several minor late antique items: Gregory of Nyssa's encomia, Chrysostom, Basil's letters, the Codex Theodosianus extract (Марей 2017), Justinian's Corpus extracts, Gelasius of Cyzicus, the Syro-Roman lawbook and Kosmas' wider text.
- The parser missed some links where the HTML has «<a» on one line and «href» on the next. Some authors may therefore have more publications on vostlit than shown here.
- Several "complete" verdicts were not checked chapter by chapter: Theodore Lector, Ps.-Arrian Periplus, the Kartir KKZ inscription, Pacatus 1997, the Peter of Alexandria Chronicle and the extent of the George Hamartolos Slavonic translation.
- Jerome's Chronicle (Дьяконов 2018) may still be incomplete online.
- Some translations were made from a modern translation rather than the original: Zonaras and Julius Africanus from English, Isidore's Chronica maiora from Spanish, and part of Isidore's History of the Goths from English.
- vostlit hosts no Alexander Romance (Ps.-Callisthenes, Julius Valerius, Armenian or Syriac versions). Alexander material appears only inside other texts: Mroveli (Nectanebo version), the Karnamag (opens with Alexander's death), Shahrestaniha, Tarikh-i Sistan, the Dinawari excerpt (Шмидт 1958), and Ibn Khurradadhbih's account of Alexander's wall.

On the «Памятники письменности Востока» series: per the ru.wikipedia volume list through CLXVII, it contains no Syriac chronicles, no late-antique Armenian historians and no Arabic universal histories with Alexander sections. Its relevant late-antique or Iranian volumes are LXXVIII, XCIV, CXIV, CXV, CXIX, CXXVI, XXXIII/1, XLII, LXVIII and LXXXIII. The Armenian volumes in the series are all medieval (Аристакэс, Киракос, Канакерци, Нарекаци, Даврижеци). The Syriac and Armenian late-antique translations listed above appeared elsewhere: Ереван editions, Труды ИВ, ВДИ, ВВ and Pigulevskaya's monographs. I took the PPV volume numbers from Wikipedia without checking the physical volumes. The Wikipedia list prints «LVIII» for Hisham al-Kalbi (between LXVII and LXIX in sequence); I assume this is a typo for LXVIII and gave it that way.

The standard edition is C. Wendel, "Scholia in Theocritum vetera" (Leipzig: Teubner, 1914), which also contains the scholia on the technopaegnia, the Prolegomena and the Anecdoton Estense.
